newsitem.title: JAPAN: Parties scuffle as Japan election hits final round.
newsitem.headline: Parties scuffle as Japan election hits final round.

text.p: Japan's two biggest political parties got into a scuffle over a newspaper advertisement on Monday as the nation's general election campaign entered the final rounds.

The main opposition Shinshinto (New Frontier Party) made a formal complaint to prosecutors over what it called "illegal wording" in the ad by the biggest party in the ruling coalition, the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP).
The ad, which has run in several national newspapers ahead of next Sunday's polls, taunted Shinshinto over its election promise to keep the sales tax at the current three percent.

"Which is the real Shinshinto?" asked the ad, saying party leader Ichiro Ozawa had proposed a rise in the tax to 10 percent while senior Shinshinto member Morihiro Hosokawa had mentioned seven percent and another, Tsutomu Hata, 15 percent.
"The LDP advertisement distorts the facts and leads citizens to misunderstand our party's platform," Shinshinto Secretary-General Takeo Nishioka said in a statement.
"It violates the fairness clause in the Public Office Election Law," Nishioka said.
Legal complaints do not automatically mean an investigation and it is up to state prosecutors to take up such motions. But the move is a formal, legal step.

In the complaint, Shinshinto also accused the LDP of distributing an "illegal" pamphlet and asked the LDP to publicly explain why it was trying to raise the sales tax to five percent from three percent.
"Our party's political activities have been recognised as lawful and we have confirmed this," LDP Secretary-General Koichi Kato said in a statement after receiving notice of the opposition complaint.
"Our party will take firm legal action against this complaint and we are now consulting our attorneys," Kato added.
Ex-premiers Hosokawa and Hata are senior members of Shinshinto. Ozawa has mentioned a 10 percent sales tax as a possibility, but it is not part of a formal election platform.
While in office in 1994, Hosokawa had proposed replacing the three percent sales tax with a seven percent "welfare tax" but withdrew his proposal after severe criticism.
Hata never mentioned a 15 percent sales tax while in office but has written that a huge income tax cut could be replaced by a big sales tax.
Neither Hata nor Hosokawa were Shinshinto members when they aired their views and neither has opposed the party's current policy of keeping the sales tax at three percent.
